Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; one of the main indicators of the strength of a nation's economy is the extent to which the prices of the basic items people need for living are kept stable. Looking at this, we did important work last year. Accordingly, we increased the number of basic food items to 23 and ensured they would be available at good prices in the Male' market. And arrangements are now being made to supply these 23 items at STO's rate, with an announcement made to find STO agents to supply goods to islands with populations of three thousand. In addition, STO has begun importing these 23 basic food items directly from abroad to Addu City and Kulhudhuffushi City. As a result, the 23 basic items will be available in those cities at the same price as Male'. At the same time, an STO distribution centre has been opened at Male' port. And an STO outlet will be established in Hulhumale' before the start of Ramadan this year. In addition, a duty-free zone for storing goods was established at Kulhudhuffushi port on 26 August last year. And, God willing, I will establish such a duty-free zone at Addu port and begin providing services within this month.

The work of the first phase of relocating Male's commercial port to Thilafushi is also important work in this regard. The work on the 125-metre international quay wall, the most important work in the first phase, will be handed over by MPL to a party today. And the work on the two-kilometre quay wall, paving and constructing buildings needed to relocate the domestic port to Thilafushi, and procuring equipment, will be handed over to various parties by the middle of this year. Completing all this work, God willing, I will relocate Male's commercial port to Thilafushi on 11 November 2027. With this change, once port services begin, a boat that currently takes 7 days to unload will be unloaded within 48 hours, the period goods can be kept at the port will be extended, and the cost of bringing goods to the Maldives will fall. With all these changes, the price of goods will be reduced and the benefit will reach the people. And opportunities will open to warehouse in Thilafushi goods currently warehoused in Male', and the wholesale trade now carried on in the Male' market area will be relocated to Thilafushi practically in its entirety. Cargo vessels will be able to dock easily, the days they must wait at port to load and unload will be reduced, and taking goods to the islands will be faster. And the difficulties the public faces because goods must be warehoused in various parts of Male' will be resolved, and the market area, now the busiest in Male', and the MPL area will become easier for vehicles and an easier place for people to walk about; God willing, it will change in that way. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; in expanding and developing the Maldives' economy, in addition to the policy of advancing small and medium enterprises, it is this government's policy to broaden good opportunities for large Maldivian and foreign businesses as well. And making the Maldivian economy a trustworthy environment with an appetite for foreign investment is something the government gives very high priority. Accordingly, as a result of the work done last year, 54 foreign investments have been registered in the Maldives. Looking at the notable large investments, I highlight the world-famous Google's international submarine cable project "Dhivaru". This project shows that, because of the economic reforms this government is bringing, the confidence of the world's largest technology companies is also coming to the Maldives. At the same time, the Aila project, begun in N. Atoll on 29 January 2026 under the sustainable township concept, is the largest investment the private sector has made in the Maldives to date. This investment, which invests 790 million dollars in its first phase, will, God willing, become an investment that brings very great growth to the Maldivian economy.

Likewise, to make room for the tourism industry, which is changing at a fast pace, a programme named Maldives Pearl Residence has been introduced, and Henley and Partners, a world-renowned firm, has been entrusted with running and promoting the programme. This is a residency visa given in return for investing in designated industries under principles set by the government. It is a programme aimed at issuing this residency visa and securing great sustainable economic benefit for the Maldives in the long term. Because of this programme, the share of foreign currency circulating in the Maldives will increase, the capital to be invested will increase, new industrial activities will be created, and the way will be paved for progress in the Maldives. Work on drafting the legal framework of this programme, with the help of this Honourable Majlis, is now under way. The government's aim is to fully launch this programme in the coming month of April and begin accepting applications through the programme. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; in advancing and diversifying the Maldivian economy, increasing the number of educationally qualified young Maldivians and Maldivians of various age groups is, in my view, a very important matter connected to the development and civilisation of Maldivians. Therefore, an inclusive employment policy prioritising Maldivians has been drafted, and for the first time in the Maldives a National Human Capital Needs Analysis has been carried out and has now been published. Accordingly, last year Maldives Polytechnic ran training programmes in the fields the government designated as fields reserved for Maldivians and including many more technical fields. Targeting various fields of national development, 852 scholarship opportunities were given and loans were given to 880 students. Likewise, work has begun to review the technical and vocational educational programmes conducted through the school system and to build the workers needed for the Maldives' economic sectors. Accordingly, to broaden the higher secondary stage and make the young people who will be active in tomorrow's workplace a productive people, a vocational education stream has been introduced at the higher secondary stage. At the same time, we have established a vocational high school in the Maldives for the first time. This is an important part of the work the government has been doing to raise the nation's human capital. And I note that it has been arranged in this academic year that has begun to expand the work of the vocational high school I mentioned and carry forward work to train more students in the fields the nation needs.

In addition, broadening higher education throughout the Maldives for young people and those of various age groups, and arranging for study opportunities to be available from every atoll, is an important measure that must be taken in achieving sustainable development. Among the work done in this regard, a project to establish higher education campuses in all atolls that currently have no government institution providing higher education and training has begun for the first time in the history of the Maldives. Accordingly, 26 projects of the Maldives National University in 16 atolls and 12 projects of the Islamic University of Maldives in 10 atolls are under way. In addition, to facilitate technical education and training opportunities, a project to construct technical vocational centres in 10 atolls and 14 projects to establish accommodation facilities are under way. At the same time, the First Degree Scheme gave opportunities to an additional 2728 students last year, and financial assistance of nine hundred and twenty-one thousand six hundred and thirty-six rufiyaa; nine hundred and twenty-one million six hundred and thirty-six thousand six hundred and fifty-seven rufiyaa was disbursed to a total of 11252 students [unclear: the figure is stated twice in the minutes with differing amounts]. In addition, for the first time in the history of the Maldives, in line with Islamic Sharia, the administrative fee charged on top of the loan amount on student loans issued by the government so far has been completely stopped. In addition, to resolve the difficulty of obtaining dollars faced by students pursuing education abroad, the card limit has been increased so that students studying abroad can withdraw twelve hundred dollars a month. As a way of bringing an adequate solution to the challenges and concerns these students face in obtaining the services they must receive from the relevant government offices, the "Kuri" system introduced on the 3rd of this month is a modern system that modernises the services provided to students and changes work that had been done manually to modern automation. Accordingly, the biggest convenience students will get from the "Kuri" system is a permanent solution to the difficulties they face in obtaining money. Accordingly, the manual payment voucher practice followed until now will be abandoned and it will be linked directly to SAP, the government's financial system. As a result, documents will be completed, the way will be paved for money to be deposited immediately without delay, and, God willing, students will be able to see in real time how their payments are being processed. In addition, an end can also be brought to the long wait required to check whether a loan's conditions are met. With the help of a modern automated workflow, from the point an application is submitted, whether the student is enrolled in another course and whether they are blacklisted can be verified instantly through the system.

At the same time, under the "verify once" principle, God willing, a student's certificates and information will need to be verified only once in their entire life. With this, there will be no need to submit documents anew each time, and, God willing, obtaining the service will become easier and faster. The "Kuri" system has also brought this speed to the student selection stage. Accordingly, the manual evaluation practised before will be ended, and from the point an application is submitted, automated evaluation will proceed and, through "one-click awarding", the students obtaining the highest marks will be selected instantly and award letters generated. And to save the errors that arise when agreements are drafted manually and the time spent on it, agreements and payment schedules will be prepared automatically. With this, students will be able to sign the agreement electronically through a digital link and apply for the money immediately. And, to resolve the difficulties faced in dealings and eliminate the burden of waiting for emails that go unanswered, questions will be answered instantly in Dhivehi and English through the AI chatbot included in the "Kuri" system. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; as a result of the policies set and being implemented to increase the number of educationally qualified young Maldivians and Maldivians of various age groups in order to advance and diversify the Maldivian economy, 21174 job opportunities have been created in the Maldivian economy from 17 November 2023 to today. This includes 7724 jobs the Pension Office says were created in the private sector. At the same time, I announce that, after consultation in the Cabinet, it has been decided that twelve months from today, from 5 February 2027, only Maldivians may work as cashiers anywhere in the Maldives. As a result, at least fifty thousand additional job opportunities will open to Maldivians within the coming year. To make this a success, I give full assurance that within the coming year the government will give all possible assistance in building people, instilling care for work, raising awareness about work ethics, and, together with business owners, preparing those business owners for this. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

The full results of the work done to increase job opportunities for Maldivians, especially young Maldivians, will come, and its lasting positive change will reach the nation's economy, only by resolving the problem of foreigners living in the Maldives illegally. This government began a 3-year operation to resolve this problem. In this operation, carried out under the name "Kurangi" Operation, the biometrics of two hundred and five thousand seven hundred and one foreigners, including ten-finger prints and photos needed for facial recognition, have so far been taken and updated. If a foreigner living without giving biometrics and without a work permit is now identified, that person can be sent away immediately. Accordingly, from 17 November 2025 to 31 January 2026, 228 foreigners living illegally in the Maldives without giving biometrics have been sent away. And from 17 November 2023 to 3 February 2026, 11496 foreigners living illegally in the Maldives have been sent away. Looking at it this way, only 2649 foreigners were sent away between 2018 and 2023. At the same time, the second phase of the Kurangi Operation has now also begun. The programme to legalise foreigners who gave biometrics but have not been legalised, which is scheduled to proceed under this phase, began on 1 January 2026. Under this programme, 3837 applications for legalisation have been received so far. In addition, God willing, the third phase of the Kurangi Operation will begin on 3 May 2026. Under this phase, through work done jointly by the police, councils and immigration on every island of the Maldives, foreign workers who are not regularised and living without a valid work permit in various parts of the Maldives will be deported without being given any further opportunity. With the help of Almighty Allah, when this operation ends on 52 May 2027 [unclear: date as printed], if there are foreigners living illegally in the Maldives, their correct number and who they are can be established. And, God willing, a credible, permanent solution will be found to the problem of foreigners living illegally in the Maldives. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; one industry to which the government gives the highest priority in working to strengthen the nation's economy is the tourism industry. Tourism is the backbone of the Maldivian economy. It is the main gateway through which foreign currency enters the Maldives. Last year notable progress was achieved in the tourism sector. Accordingly, by the end of last year, 2.2 million tourists visited the Maldives. This is growth of 9.8% compared to 2024. According to Maldives Monetary Authority statistics, revenue of 5.55 billion US dollars was received from the tourism industry last year. This is growth of 13.8% compared to the previous year. The Maldives

Monetary Authority estimates that revenue of 5.6 billion dollars will be received from tourism this year. The government's aim is to increase the number of tourists visiting the Maldives this year to 2.5 million, achieving growth of 11.3%. To achieve this, the government's aim is to make promoting the Maldives a work in which everyone takes part. To achieve this purpose, I declare and announce 2027 as "Visit Maldives Year". This will be, God willing, a major national campaign carried out jointly by all parties in and outside the Maldives directly and indirectly connected with the tourism industry. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; in 2023 not a single resort, nor a single tourist hotel, opened in the Maldives. However, over the past two years a total of 6535 tourist beds have been added to the tourism industry. This includes 1474 beds added by three resorts opened last year and three resorts opened in 2024, 708 beds added by three tourist hotels opened over the past two years, 3574 beds added by 194 guesthouses opened, 463 beds added by 22 tourist vessels launched, and 316 beds added by homestays. In addition, 391 brand-new travel agencies and 45 dive centres have been registered and have begun operating. And it is estimated that an additional seven resorts and guesthouses will be added to the tourism industry this year. Spreading the benefits of the tourism industry to the whole of the Maldives is one of the government's aims. Accordingly, investments have been opened with special concessions to expand tourism, including halal tourism, in 6 atolls where tourism has not so far developed as desired. To date, 8 sites among these have been awarded. And lease agreements have been signed for 6 sites. In addition, one halal tourism island has been leased. And special work was done last year to develop tourism in Addu Atoll. Accordingly, the Shangri-La resort, which had been closed, has now been opened. This is the result of work the government did together with that resort's management. The Addu Hankede project, which had stalled without progressing, has also been re-awarded to develop integrated tourism. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

The tourism industry officially began in the Maldives 54 years ago, in 1972. However, even after more than half a century of this industry, no government has paved any way for even a single laari from this sector to reach the pockets of all Maldivian citizens directly. But in reality this industry is the one that plays the biggest role in the Maldivian economy. It is the industry that makes the greatest long-term use of natural assets such as beautiful beaches, lagoons, reefs and islands, which are the natural beauty of the Maldives, and which has brought and is bringing major changes to those assets that, except in few cases, cannot be reversed. Therefore, I believe that the fairest course is for a way to be systematically established for all the beloved Maldivian citizens, the true owners of these natural assets, to receive a direct income. Accordingly, after consultation in the Cabinet on this, the government has now decided to develop at least 10 resorts through a government company within the next three years, and to deposit a large part of the profits from those resorts, without leaving out a single citizen, equally, once a year, in foreign currency, into the bank account of every citizen of the Maldives. And to establish by law that every citizen of the Maldives is, equally, a shareholder of every resort developed under this project. As a result, the profits from the resorts developed under this project will reach every citizen holding a Maldivian identity card equally year after year, and for the first time in the history of the Maldives every Maldivian citizen will become a direct shareholder in Maldivian tourism, and, God willing, financial benefit will begin to be deposited directly to every Maldivian citizen. It is estimated that money from this investment will begin to be deposited into citizens' accounts from 2030. By calculation, God willing, an average of at least 400 dollars a year will be deposited into every citizen's account. For example, in a family of five members, in addition to every member of that family becoming a shareholder of at least ten resorts, God willing, that family will receive at least two thousand US dollars a year. God willing, I will carry forward with great speed all the things that must be done to make this a reality. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; in developing the Maldives' tourism industry, it is essential to develop airports, increase the airlines and routes flying to and from the Maldives and within the Maldives, and establish a strong transport network by air, sea and land. At the same time, it is also very important for a strong transport network by air, sea and land to be established for the people of the Maldives to travel and to expand trade and the economy. And likewise,

in the Maldivian context, for the purpose of climate adaptation too, establishing a strong transport network by air, sea and land in the Maldives' circumstances is nothing other than a necessity. Accordingly, among the results achieved, the new terminal of Velana International Airport opened on 26 July 2025, and Hanimaadhoo International Airport was also developed and opened on 9 November 2025. The Maldives' national airline "Maldivian" introduced wide-body aircraft operations and began commercial operations to three destinations in China from 22 January last year. God willing, a second wide-body aircraft will be brought in and put into operation this year. In addition, Maafaru International Airport has been further developed, and the runway and apron have been enlarged to a level able to serve large aircraft such as the Boeing 777 and Airbus A350. And the project to enlarge the airport's terminal has also now begun. Muli airport, established in M. Muli, was opened on 8 May 2025 and this airport's service has also begun. In addition, much work on developing airports in various parts of the Maldives is under way at various stages. Accordingly, work on developing the airports at HA. Dhidhdhoo, HDh. Makunudhoo, Sh. Bilehfahi, Sh. Komandoo, Sh. Milandhoo, N. Vihafaru, R. Alifushi, R. Fainu, B. Thulhaadhoo, AA. Mathiveri, F. Nilandhoo, F. Magoodhoo, Th. Guraidhoo, Th. Vilufushi, L. Kadhdhoo, GA. Vilingili, GDh. Kaadedhdhoo and Addu Gan, and upgrading the airports at HA. Hoarafushi, HDh. Kulhudhuffushi, Sh. Funadhoo, GA. Maavarulu and Fuvahmulah City, is under way at various stages. I also note that, as a result of the work done so far to upgrade airports, all airports operating in the Maldives have now been developed to allow night flights to land and have begun being used. And, God willing, the work of transferring B. Dharavandhoo airport to Island Aviation will be completed by the end of this month, and the work of developing the airport will begin very soon. Likewise, God willing, work on building a second airport in L. Atoll will also begin this year. In addition, from 1 February this year, flights on twin otter aircraft on wheels have begun to Addu Atoll Gan, Fuvahmulah City and Huvadhu Atoll. This is the integrated air connectivity network linking the integrated development zone of the four southernmost atolls announced under the sustainable development policy. Likewise, in the integrated development zone of the three northernmost atolls, an integrated air connectivity network linking HA. Hoarafushi, HA. Dhidhdhoo, HDh. Kulhudhuffushi, HDh. Hanimaadhoo and HDh. Makunudhoo will be established once all these airports are completed.

Likewise, under the project carried forward to expand seaplane services specifically for the tourism industry and generally for all citizens, flights to N. Velidhoo began on 22 January this year. And flights to AA. Thoddoo will begin within this month. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; under the work done to establish a quality sea transport system, speed ferry service began in three atolls last year. And, God willing, speed ferry service will be established within the next 6 months in the 8 atolls where the service has not been established. This system can be made a sustainable, successful system only by also raising the standard of the islands' coastal infrastructure. Accordingly, through the work done so far, the work on fourteen harbour projects has been completed. And, together with 33 projects newly signed last year, work on 102 harbour projects is now under way at various stages in various parts of the Maldives. And within this year harbour work on an additional sixteen islands will be handed over. God willing, I will complete and hand over these 118 harbour projects within the next 19 months. To achieve this result, and to reduce costs, the relevant government ministries and companies have jointly begun special work to bring in the rock boulders needed for the work in bulk and stockpile them in the Maldives. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; among the work the government is doing to establish quality, sustainable land transport infrastructure, road works on 6 islands were completed this past year. And, together with 57 projects newly signed last year, work on 97 road projects is under way at various stages in various parts of the Maldives. Within this year road work on an additional thirteen islands will be handed over. God willing, I will complete and hand over the road projects of these 110 islands within the next 22 months. In road building, it has been decided to build sand roads with a quality drainage system, as requested by the people of many islands where local tourism is growing. To speed up the carrying out of road projects and to resolve the problem of project costs rising because various machinery and equipment must be rented, all the relevant modern machinery and equipment, enough to do the work of many islands at once at low cost in-house, will be brought to the Roads Development Corporation before the end of April this year. Of the machinery brought in this way, one

set-up will be mobilised to Gulhifalhu, and, God willing, with all the relevant government ministries and companies working together, I will begin the water, sewerage, electricity and road works of Gulhifalhu in May this year. Likewise, once the reclamation of Giraavarufalhu is completed, an additional set-up will be taken to Giraavarufalhu, and, God willing, I will begin the water, sewerage, electricity and road works of Giraavarufalhu in the middle of this year. In addition, it has been arranged to begin early this year the design work of the project to redevelop the roads of Male' and Vilimale', which is to be done with grant aid from the Government of China. And it is expected that the physical work will begin late this year. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; one of the biggest works closely tied to road building is water and sewerage work. Since 17 November 2023, water systems have been established and begun providing service on 42 islands, and sewerage systems have been established and begun providing service on 39 islands. Therefore, once water systems are established on an additional 51 islands and sewerage systems on 40 islands, water and sewerage systems will have been established on every island of the Maldives. God willing, I will complete all these projects and begin providing water and sewerage services to every inhabited island within the next eighteen months. God willing, the work on the water production system included in the project carried forward to develop the water service of Addu City, the most populous after Male', will be completed and begin providing service before the end of April this year. Under the work done to ensure the security of the Male' area's water service, the water networks of Male' and Hulhumale' have been linked via the Sinamale' Bridge and have now begun to be used. And, under the work done to increase water storage capacity in the Male' area, work on a ten-thousand-tonne tank was completed last year and it has now begun to be used. In addition, the physical work of placing two thirteen-thousand-tonne tanks in Male' has also now begun. And the physical work of an additional thirteen thousand tonnes of water storage, targeting the growing population of Hulhumale', will begin this year. When this work is completed in 2027, God willing, the water storage capacity of the Male' area will increase by 130%. In addition, while water production in the Male' area was increased by 16% during 2025, with the completion of the five-thousand-tonne work now under way by March this year, God willing, water production capacity in the Male' area will increase by 25%. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

Looking after such infrastructure established on every island of the Maldives properly, that is, maintaining it under a proper maintenance schedule, is work that must be done when considered sustainably, in terms of cost, in a sustainable way, and in terms of recurring cost. Accordingly, to expand public works services to the atolls, public works units with the most modern facilities will be established by the middle of this year on 19 islands in the 15 atolls where that service has not yet been established. Once this arrangement is in place, among maintaining the infrastructure established on the islands, the work of deepening harbour basins when they silt up, deepening harbour entrances when they silt up, carrying out various harbour repairs, repairing roads, and the maintenance and repair of buildings and various infrastructure can, God willing, be carried forward faster than now, at very low cost, and very reliably. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; in developing the nation in the area of infrastructure development, the government's policy is always to prioritise sustainable development. Sustainable development can be prioritised only by designing development work in a way that protects our fragile environment. For this, the government is carrying out important climate adaptation work. Unusual erosion is one of the biggest environmental problems faced by the islands of the Maldives. To find a solution to this problem, a national coastal zone management policy has been drafted. And information on the changes that occurred between 2015 and 2023 to the beaches of every inhabited island in the Maldives has been compiled using remote sensing and artificial intelligence. Among the coastal protection projects carried out last year to address erosion, the work on 6 islands has been fully completed. Together with fourteen projects newly signed during last year, a total of 62 coastal protection projects are under way at various stages. And coastal protection work will begin on an additional 15 islands this year. God willing, I will complete and hand over these 77 projects within the next eighteen months. At the same time, the lack of an adequate, robust waste management system on many islands is something because of which citizens have had to bear great hardship. Therefore, the work of establishing waste management centres on 135 islands where such centres have not been established has been handed over, with the agreements signed. God willing, all of these

islands' work will be carried forward, and I will complete and hand over the work on all these islands within the next fifteen months. In addition, to protect the environment and to make the Maldivian environment a greener one, a project to plant five million trees in the Maldives by 2028 has begun as a special climate mitigation project. To date, 1.5 million trees have been planted under this project. Plans have been made and arrangements put in place to plant an additional one million trees this year, 1.5 million trees in 2027 and one million trees in 2028. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; in strengthening and advancing the Maldivian economy, special attention must be given to fisheries, the lifeblood of the Maldivian economy. The fisheries industry, which had been neglected and impoverished for many years, is the most powerful industry handed down to us by our ancestors. It was this government that brought this neglect and exclusion to an end. Accordingly, God willing, this government will proceed firmly in bringing brightness to the fisheries industry by listening closely to the voices of fishermen. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; one of the biggest challenges facing the fisheries industry is the low cold storage capacity for storing fresh fish. As a way of resolving this, God willing, I will complete and hand over within the next 15 months the projects to establish cold storage in GDh. Thinadhoo City, Lh. Felivaru, M. Mulah, GA. Kooddoo, Addu Hulhudhoo, HA. Ihavandhoo, GDh. Fiyoari and F. Nilandhoo. To supply the ice fishermen need, new ice plants have been established in GA. Dhevvadhoo, Sh. Funadhoo, Dh. Meedhoo and Bandidhoo [unclear: atoll prefix not given] and have now begun providing service. God willing, the work on the ice plants of M. Veyvah and L. Maabaidhoo will be completed by the middle of this year and they will begin providing service. And, God willing, I will complete the work of building ice plants in HA. Dhidhdhoo, AA. Rasdhoo, GDh. Rathafandhoo, HDh. Kulhudhuffushi, GA. Vilingili, GA. Nilandhoo, K. Gaafaru, Dh. Hulhudheli, Sh. Komandoo, Lh. Naifaru, L. Maavah and L. Hithadhoo and begin providing service this year. To encourage installing refrigerated seawater, or RSW, systems on fishing vessels, facilities for 45 parties have been approved so far and 25 million rufiyaa disbursed. And, targeting an additional 200

fishing vessels, SME Digital has opened RSW financing to applications. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; another of the biggest difficulties fishermen face is the difficulty of obtaining fuel at a good price in all regions of the Maldives. Among the work the government is doing to resolve this, to arrange for fuel to be available at STO rates, STO's first fuel skid was opened in R. Dhuvaafaru on 13 December 2025. God willing, STO fuel skids will open in every atoll of the Maldives within the next three months. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; since 10 December 2024 the money owed to fishermen has been paid within 48 hours. Accordingly, from 10 December 2024 without interruption to 3 February 2026, one thousand and sixteen million three hundred and twenty-nine thousand three hundred and seventy-six rufiyaa has been disbursed. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; work is also being done to find solutions to the concerns and challenges of yellowfin tuna fishermen. Arrangements are being made to supply fuel at a good price to yellowfin tuna fishermen too, in the same way as skipjack tuna fishermen. Since yellowfin tuna fishermen will get a good return only by establishing a modern packing facility needed by companies exporting tuna, God willing, I will begin the physical work of building such a facility in Hulhumale' this year. For this, the agreement for the fifty-thousand-square-foot plot needed to build the hundred-tonne packing facility arranged to be established in Hulhumale' has been signed, and, God willing, the physical work on this facility will begin by the middle of this year. And the work the government must do to purchase yellowfin tuna is also progressing very vigorously. The government's aim is to develop yellowfin tuna fishing and increase the economic benefit from yellowfin tuna fishing beyond what it was before. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

FADs are a resource that plays an important role in the fisheries industry. For that reason, further expanding the FAD network is this government's policy. Work is being done to change the design to reduce the rate at which FADs break away and to further look into ways to extend the life of FADs. I note that under the project to deploy deep-sea FADs and nearshore FADs, 41 FADs were deployed last year, making 2025 the year in which the most FADs have been established in a single year to date. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; I regard the National Fishermen's Registry established by this government to ensure the social and economic security of fishermen as a very great advance for this sector. I note with pleasure that 100% of the vessels operating in fisheries are now included in this registry. Because of this registry, fishermen have today begun to receive the services of financial facilities. Accordingly, loans totalling 10.4 million rufiyaa have so far been issued to 80 parties through Bank of Maldives. At the same time, to include fishermen in the financial sector, arrangements have now also been made for fishermen registered in the National Fishermen's Registry to easily obtain loans and financing based on their income for various purposes such as personal financing, credit cards, buying, building and repairing homes, and educating fishermen's children. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; to provide financial assistance to businesses operating in the fisheries industry, we introduced a new financing scheme named "Mahaa Manfaa" among the activities of last year's Fishermen's Day. Under this scheme, financing assistance of between fifty thousand and four hundred thousand will be available for cooking and drying fish, packaging products, and establishing fish storage systems. And arrangements have also been made to finance 200 boats, providing concessional loans between eighty thousand rufiyaa and six hundred and forty thousand rufiyaa on Islamic principles. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; with the changes coming to the fisheries environment, K. Bodduhfaru, V. Maadhiggarufalhu, GDh. Bolimathaidhoo and GA. Maafaru have been designated as special areas to develop sports fishing, and this was announced on last year's Fishermen's Day. Before beginning to establish sports fishing harbours in these areas,

God willing, I will submit to this Honourable Majlis during the first session of this year an amendment that must be made to the law. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; as a way of expanding further branches of fisheries, five special zones for mariculture work have been designated. They are Bodu Thiladhunmathi, R. Atoll, K. Atoll, M. Atoll and Th. Atoll. It has been arranged to give major concessions to those investing in these areas, with no acquisition fee and no rent payable for the first three years. At the same time, the work on the multi-species hatchery now under way in GA. Maanagala will be completed, and, God willing, its services will formally begin this year. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; I regard agriculture as an industry in the Maldivian economy to which governments have not so far given adequate attention, but which, thinking from a sustainable development perspective, is one that needs the most attention. To establish a resilient economy, it is this government's policy to work to produce the main kinds of food produced in the Maldives in quantities adequate for the population of the Maldives and to establish food security. To reach this aim, a very favourable environment for agricultural investments has now been established. And work has now begun to increase agricultural businesses and bring private sector investment to this sector. Under a "Public Private Partnership", Kondey and Kaashidhoo have now been opened for starting an agricultural project. And, God willing, I will open L. Gan and HDh. Nolhivaranfaru this year to carry work forward. These projects will work to develop sustainable agriculture on the islands and to find solutions to the challenges faced by island-level farmers, such as difficulties in buying and selling produce. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; I believe that sustainable, meaningful, inclusive development can be brought to the nation only by designing policy that regards achieving social development alongside economic development as two intertwined things, and working accordingly. This is my policy. Making this proud Maldivian nation a country where citizens live who are educationally capable, healthy, physically fit, psychologically strong and morally of good character is my pride. My responsibility. My duty. Into such a society

for our society to become is also an absolute necessity in making it an economically resilient, socially stable, safe nation. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; an educationally capable generation can be built only by raising the standard of school education. By bringing sustainable positive changes to the education system. By doing sincere work to resolve the many matters neglected and abandoned in the education sector until now. This government has begun that work. Accordingly, since the learning of students at the primary education stage has not been robustly measured, to identify the extent to which students completing this stage are achieving the outcomes set in the national curriculum, a special exam named the "National Curriculum Examination" began to be given last year, targeting grade 6 students completing primary education. At the same time, to assess the level of students completing the primary education stage and benchmark it internationally, the Assessment of Minimum Proficiency Level exam was piloted for the first time last year for students who completed Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2. This year this exam will be carried out in schools across the Maldives. With the results of this exam, the level of Maldivian students can be compared with students of other countries. In addition, with the review of primary education textbooks and the preparation of a curriculum integration model, work has begun to rewrite the books of Key Stage 1 students as thematic books. The result will be that the lessons studied in various subjects are linked, and learning and teaching are shaped to make it easier for students to learn the lessons. In addition, in line with Maldives 2.0, a digitalised system for easily managing education sector information will be established in this academic year. The result will be paving the way to formulate and implement decisions related to learning and teaching based on real-time and accurate information. For this, God willing, I will carry forward this year the work of establishing digital infrastructure and equipment in all schools of the Maldives. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; as part of providing infrastructure in schools, by December last year the work on 142 classrooms and 9 multipurpose halls, as well as the construction of 56 educational support facilities such as science labs, libraries and staff rooms, had been completed. And for this academic year, an additional 216 classrooms, 7 multipurpose halls, and 250

educational support facilities have been completed and begun to be used. At the same time, work on an additional 955 classrooms, 78 multipurpose halls and 2923 educational support facilities is currently under way in various parts of the Maldives. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; my policy is to establish fairness in the education sector as well. Every Maldivian child is equal before me. No child shall be deprived of their rights because of a disability they have. Accordingly, God willing, I will begin this year a special project to implement inclusive education, the policy of educating all students together, in its broadest sense. Looking at it this way, the difficulty of obtaining teachers to teach students with disabilities is the biggest challenge faced in this. To resolve this, through the national programme for training teachers, a programme to train teachers to teach students who need special assistance in learning began last year. This programme will be further expanded this year. In addition, God willing, this year I will complete in all schools that lack them the special classrooms needed to provide education to students who need special assistance, special educational support facilities such as special toilets designed to provide privacy taking account of those children's conditions, and the equipment, devices and other relevant resources needed for learning and teaching. Among these, God willing, I will begin this year to plan and implement the preparation of special books in various subjects for children with disabilities and special work to prepare those children for O level in a manner suited to their disability. In addition, God willing, I will submit to this Honourable Majlis in the first session of this year an amendment to the law to facilitate a homeschooling pathway for such children, in accordance with a regulation to be set, based on an assessment made looking at the degree of the student's disability or the extent of their psychological condition. Likewise, God willing, from 1 March this year, parents of children with disabilities who work in the civil service will get the opportunity to change to working from home. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; making every Maldivian citizen a healthy citizen is one of the most important foundations of this government's development policy. Accordingly, the health sector can be developed comprehensively only by

giving equal attention to the policy of preventing disease (preventive health care) and the policy of curing disease by giving proper treatment when ill (curative health care), and implementing both policies on the broadest scale, equitably, so as to include all citizens; this is what I believe. And I regard working to end the long-standing need for all citizens of the Maldives to depend on Male' to obtain health services, and also working to reduce the extent to which people have to go abroad for health services, as the fairest solution to be achieved in developing this sector. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; among the work this government has begun to protect the public health of Maldivians is establishing GP and urban primary healthcare centres in the Male' area. Accordingly, the first centre established has been opened in Male'. God willing, I will open such clinics in Hulhumale' Phase 2 and 1, and in two more areas of Male', this year. In addition, it has been decided to establish and begin this year the capability to carry out analyses to check the levels of pesticide residues and heavy metals in food. Among the work against tobacco use, we have amended the Tobacco Control Act and begun implementing a generational ban on tobacco use. We have arranged for tobacco cessation services to be available on every island of the Maldives and trained 433 health workers in this service. We have arranged to supply nicotine replacement therapy, used to stop tobacco use, to all parts of the Maldives through the Aasandha scheme. And so far 2003 citizens have taken part in the tobacco cessation programme, and 375 citizens have successfully quit tobacco use. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; because of many years of neglect without maintenance, ambulances on many islands were broken down and in a state beyond repair. Therefore, a project to provide new ambulances in place of those ambulances was begun, and so far 56 ambulances have been brought to Male' and have now been handed over to the islands. God willing, I will carry forward the work of bringing an additional 31 ambulances and 10 paramedic ambulances to Male' in March this year and sending them to the islands. Likewise, major work has also begun to strengthen the Maldives' sea ambulance system run by the MNDF. Accordingly, while some aged sea ambulances have been repaired and brought into usable condition, an additional 12 sea ambulances will be

put into service this year. Accordingly, the first sea ambulance put into service this year has now been stationed in N. Velidhoo and has begun providing service. And to expand the in-house capability of the air ambulance service, all arrangements were made last year to allow air ambulance trips to 4 countries abroad. Accordingly, on 16 November 2025 all arrangements were made for transporting patients by air ambulance at government expense to the UAE, Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore, and the agreement was signed. To increase the capability of the domestic air ambulance service, God willing, I will begin a medical evacuation helicopter service this year. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; this government has ended the earlier situation in which people with thalassaemia were not cared for as the government should care for them, and has begun resolving the matters that needed to be resolved. Accordingly, all the work needed to run a thalassaemia centre in Hulhumale's Orange Hiyaa was completed in a short time as a national task of the MNDF, and the thalassaemia centre, which had been falling into ruin, has been moved to Orange Hiyaa. And its operation has been handed over to Male' City Group of Hospitals. Those children are now receiving various specialist services they did not receive before, such as endocrinology, internal medicine and haematology. And, changing the situation in which this centre had nowhere near enough staff to serve people with thalassaemia, 38 new posts have been approved and 30 staff have now been recruited. And the MRI T2-star service, a service essential for thalassaemia children and previously available only abroad, is now available at Hulhumale' Hospital. So far this service has been given to 28 parties. In addition, under the programme this government began to provide free bone marrow transplants, an additional 10 children were sent for bone marrow transplants last year. Thus, a total of 24 children have so far been given the opportunity of a free bone marrow transplant. In addition, it has been decided to give thalassaemia children an allowance of two thousand rufiyaa from this year. And an automated DNA analysis laboratory, to identify mutations of 27 types of haemoglobin in the blood when analysing types of thalassaemia to a health standard, has been established and is now ready to provide service in a government hospital for the first time. Because of this service, blood mutations that could not be identified before will be identified and the quality of analyses improved. The quality of the related blood treatment will be raised further. This service will begin to be provided in the coming week through the Maldivian Blood Services of Male' City Group of Hospitals. At the same time, God willing, work on establishing a thalassaemia hospital will begin this year.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; various kinds of therapy are among the areas in the Maldives where the most people need treatment and there are no human resources to give adequate treatment. Therefore, God willing, I will begin in March this year a national project to produce Maldivian therapists, to run courses giving degree-level education and training in the Maldives to produce 250 Maldivians in this field, and to put them into employment under an employment agreement made with the trainees. And I state that, as an immediate solution, it has been decided to bring 50 therapists from abroad within the next 6 months, including speech therapists, occupational therapists, behavioural therapists, physiotherapists and psychotherapists. And, God willing, I will begin the physical work in the middle of this year of establishing in Hulhumale' a state-of-the-art therapy centre named the National Disability Services and Therapy Centre, where therapy services of all kinds are available. And work on establishing branches of this centre in all other cities will also begin at the same time. Once these centres are established, I will review the arrangement under which Aasandha covers all costs of therapy services from 1 January this year, and arrange for a certain percentage of that expenditure to be spent so that all those services are available free and at the highest quality from these centres. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; mental health is also a very important area in the Maldives that needs a great deal of care. Under the policy set to bring an adequate solution to this, the 24-hour National Mental Health Helpline was established on 21 February 2025 and has so far served 13741 parties. And we have established and begun providing a brand-new mental health treatment service at Hulhumale' Hospital. And from 1 January this year, arrangements have been made for Aasandha to cover all mental health treatment. In addition, God willing, I will establish and begin providing mental health treatment services this year at the hospitals of some other islands of the Maldives. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; another area to which this government gives the highest priority in developing the health sector is fertility treatment. Accordingly, as a result of arranging for special treatment for health problems such as "endometriosis" and "PCOS" to be available through Aasandha, so far 1965 parties have

obtained endometriosis treatment. And 9650 parties have obtained PCOS treatment. Among those who applied to obtain "IUI" and "IVF" treatment through Aasandha and met the conditions, 68 parties completed IVF, and by the mercy of Allah IVF has succeeded for 23 parties. With the help of this service, two children were born in the Maldives on the 7th and 11th of January this year. This is a historic success achieved, for a long-standing major problem in the Maldives, without out-of-pocket cost, while staying in the Maldives with family. At the same time, I also note that a total of 30 million rufiyaa has been deposited into the Fertility Care Fund created by this government, 93 parties have obtained treatment with the help of this fund, and 20 children have been born among them. And I also note that an additional 35 parties have so far met the conditions to undergo IVF this year using this fund. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; the State Pharmaceutical and Medical Supply Corporation (State Pharma), a new company created by the government to ensure arrangements for the basic medicines the people need to be available without interruption, has now begun work to bring to the Maldives critical medicines, among those the Maldives essentially needs, that are not currently available. God willing, these medicines will begin to be available before the end of April this year. And, to arrange for medicines to be available responsibly, State Pharma has now begun work with regional and international partners. God willing, to protect the health and well-being of the people, I will ensure this year a permanent and sustainable solution to the difficulties in the medicine supply system. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; even if infrastructure and health facilities are established to develop the health sector, if there are not enough service providers to provide services using those facilities, services cannot be provided to the people as desired. Therefore, giving the health sector a priority given to no other sector in establishing human resources, jobs have so far been arranged for a total of 1711 service providers: 669 for health services in the atolls and 1042 for Male' Group of Hospitals. And, God willing, I will arrange jobs this year, with the highest priority, for a total of 1950 service providers additionally needed for the various health centres opening this year and the various services being added to hospitals. The budget needed for that is included in the health sector budget passed for this year.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; much work was done last year to strengthen health services in the atolls and expand diagnostic services. Accordingly, a major project has begun to expand radiology services, including MRI, CT scan, X-ray and ultrasound scan services. Dialysis services have been newly established and begun on 9 islands. The physical work of 143 health sector infrastructure development projects is currently under way on 143 islands in the atolls. Likewise, a great deal of work has also begun to strengthen the services provided in the Male' area. Accordingly, last year a 75-bed multi-specialty surgical ward was established at IGMH and began providing service. Accordingly, some brand-new surgeries and procedures have begun. To expand Hulhumale' Hospital's services, the number of emergency room beds and dialysis beds has been increased and services expanded. Optical shops were opened at IGMH and Hulhumale' Hospital, paving the way to get spectacles made for two thousand rufiyaa under Aasandha; as a result, so far 12988 people have had their eyes examined, and among them 12056 Maldivian citizens have had spectacles made through this system. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; among the major health projects that will begin in the Male' area this year is the physical work on the hundred-bed tertiary hospital being established in Vilimale' with grant aid from the Government of China. And, God willing, I will begin the work of establishing a five-hundred-bed multi-specialty hospital in Hulhumale' Phase 2 in the middle of this year. In addition, God willing, I will begin in the middle of this year the work of establishing a diagnostic centre dedicated to cancer services, including a radiation chamber needed for cancer treatment. At the same time, God willing, I will also begin in the middle of this year the work of building a 250-bed multi-specialty tertiary hospital as an extension of Hulhumale' Hospital. In addition, God willing, this year I will carry forward at Hulhumale' Hospital an additional MRI machine, starting urology services with urodynamic services, starting gastroenterology services with an endoscopy suite, starting neurology services including OPD and EEG services, introducing CXL surgery and expanding ophthalmology services, and establishing a dental laboratory.

And likewise, God willing, this year I will establish a separate cath lab at Dharumavantha Hospital and develop the National Cardiac Centre. And, God willing, I will begin this year cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, interventional radiology, gastro ERCP and robotic surgery services at Dharumavantha Hospital and IGMH. In addition, God willing, the "National Centre for Neuroscience and Stroke" will open at Dharumavantha Hospital within the coming week. With the opening of this centre, God willing, the treatment given in the Maldives for neurological diseases will be raised to new heights. Because of this centre, in future brain and spinal operations will be carried out with modern facilities such as robotic technology, and a system will be established through a network linking the whole of the Maldives for stroke patients to receive treatment quickly. And because of programmes run together with the atoll hospitals, the way will be paved for quality neurological treatment to be available in all regions of the Maldives. Looking at the work arranged to be carried forward in the atolls this year, it has been decided to introduce mammography services in the tertiary and regional hospitals that lack that service. And this year I will carry forward at Addu City Hospital the making of a private ward, increasing space in the admin building, establishing a mental health centre, integrating various kinds of therapy, changing OPD services to two shifts, and adding services. Likewise, God willing, this year too I will carry forward the work of providing the medical equipment needed to complete the existing services at Kulhudhuffushi Hospital, Thinadhoo Hospital, Fuvahmulah Hospital and Ungoofaaru Hospital, and of establishing all the services a complete tertiary hospital must have. At the same time, God willing, the physical work on the Fuvahmulah City, ADh. Mahibadhoo, Th. Veymandoo, L. Fonadhoo and F. Nilandhoo hospital projects, arranged to be carried out with assistance from foreign funds, will also begin this year. At the same time, laboratories will be established by the end of this year on 76 islands that have no laboratory. And an important project to replace machinery and equipment that broke down and stopped providing service because of not being maintained for many years has now been handed over to STO. God willing, this work will be completed within the next 6 months and the people will begin to receive its service. And at the same time, the work of procuring medical equipment such as MRI machines, CT machines, decompression chambers, dental equipment and X-ray machines, which must be obtained for the project to upgrade regional hospitals to tertiary level and for the projects to develop the hospitals of seven urban centres, has now

been contracted. God willing, these items will be delivered within the next seven months, this work will be completed, and the people will begin to receive those services. These are important projects that, God willing, will take health services in the atolls to a completely different level. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; in implementing the policy of preventing disease, the highest priority must be given to protecting against lifestyle-related diseases, or lifestyle diseases, and becoming physically fit citizens. To achieve this, this government regards developing the sports and fitness sector as extremely important. Accordingly, among the work done to develop the sports and fitness sector, the work on a total of 33 projects whose physical work this government began last year has been completed. And likewise, 59 projects left unfinished when this government took office were completed last year. Thus, 92 sports and fitness projects have so far been completed and handed over by this government. In addition, work on 879 sports and fitness projects begun by this government is under way at various stages in various parts of the Maldives. God willing, I will complete and hand over all these projects within the next twelve months. These include establishing and opening fitness and recreation centres on every island, and opening sixteen spacious, modern sports complexes for indoor sports with room for twelve hundred spectators on various islands of the Maldives, including the two phases of Hulhumale' and Vilimale'. Within this year, the work of building such sports complexes on an additional five islands will also be handed over. Among the other projects under way in Male' is the work of building a skate park arena with an inline speed skating or roller skating rink. This skate park arena, being established in the Male' Usfasgandu area, will become a major work done to develop the sport of skating in the Maldives. Although various skateboarding and inline speed skating activities have taken place in the Maldives since the 80s, no adequate facility has been established. This skate park arena is being established to a standard at which regional competitions can be held. God willing, I will complete this project entirely and formally open it before the end of March this year. In addition, reclamation work to establish an arena dedicated to racing and drifting will begin in March this year. And, God willing, the work of constructing in Hulhumale' a state-of-the-art multistorey futsal complex with an additional 4 indoor training pitches, including an indoor futsal stadium of a standard for holding international matches,

and a state-of-the-art multistorey netball complex with an additional 4 indoor training pitches, including an indoor netball stadium of a standard for holding international matches, will also begin in April this year. In addition, the work of establishing an e-sports centre in Male', and the work of establishing arcade games, a bowling arena and a children's indoor activities complex, will also begin in April this year. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; the policy of serving the people with equality and fairness so that no individual is left behind is the standard this government believes in when serving in every sector. Therefore, one work this government has carried forward with very high priority is improving the standard of service provided to those brought under state care for various reasons, and finding them opportunities to change their circumstances. Accordingly, through the work done to facilitate the opportunity of a family environment for children brought under state care, a family environment has so far been found for 110 children. And a programme to improve the standard of centres where children are kept and to give further training to those serving in such centres will begin this year. And the physical work on the "Empowerment Hub", being established for the purpose of empowering persons with disabilities, developing their skills and facilitating various opportunities to increase their financial well-being, began in January this year. And to facilitate job opportunities for persons with disabilities, we passed and gazetted three relevant regulations last year, and have so far given jobs to 356 persons with disabilities. The government's aim, God willing, is to arrange jobs for an additional five hundred persons with disabilities each year over the next three years. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; increasing women's share in nation building and broadening the ways for them to earn income is an important policy of this government. To economically empower women, the "Fashaa Madhadhu" loan scheme was introduced targeting women entrepreneurs, and loans have so far been arranged for 92 parties. In addition, to empower the elected women's development committees on the islands and in the cities, relevant amendments were made to the Decentralisation Act of the Maldives, and the 5% of the council budget received by the women's development committee has, from this year, been raised to 10%.

And the Ramadan allowance given to the members of those committees has been changed to be given from the council budget. At the same time, the president of the women's development committee has been made a full-time post elected by the direct vote of all citizens, and full legal empowerment has been provided for the committee president to fulfil her responsibilities and duties. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; to achieve the goal of making our society a socially safe and stable society, this government will always be a government close to the senior citizens who carried today's generations up to today. To pave the way for senior citizens to live with good health and dignity as an important part of society, and to ensure the peace of mind and well-being of senior citizens, 1185 senior citizens from thirteen atolls took part in the "Ufaaveri Raasthaa" programme begun last year. And 15213 senior citizens took part in programmes carried forward at clubs. A system will be established to carry forward this programme sustainably on every island. And among the centres this government has begun building to care for senior citizens living in the most vulnerable conditions with no one to care for them, the physical work on the centre being established in Addu City began in January this year. God willing, the work of establishing two more such centres in the north and south of the Maldives will begin this year. In addition, to facilitate the opportunity for senior citizens who wish to remain in employment up to 75 instead of compulsorily retiring at age 65, the "Re-employment" Act has been ratified, and the opportunity to work, by obtaining a contract job renewed year by year through the formal system, has now been facilitated. This will be extremely beneficial psychologically, socially and economically. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; social development and social security in the nation can be ensured only by bringing a permanent solution to the housing problem, the biggest social problem in the nation. Bringing this solution is the matter this government is working on with the highest priority. Accordingly, to make every Maldivian citizen a citizen whose right to housing is guaranteed, the "Housing for All" policy has been passed by the Cabinet and made public. Under this policy, housing opportunities within reach will open to all segments of society. For well-off families,

it includes increasing opportunities to obtain housing on real estate principles, providing middle-income families the opportunity to buy affordable homes through bank mortgages, and building social housing for families unable to buy a place on their own. And, under this "Housing for All" policy, a new programme named "Family Housing" has been started, and as the first phase of that programme, the principles for issuing fifteen thousand plots from Rasmale' and 7900 three-bedroom flats from Hulhumale' and Vilimale' to citizens living in Male' have been announced and application forms opened for submission. While the opportunity to submit forms for the family housing programme carried forward specifically for families with no housing at all has been opened, to facilitate the opportunity for all citizens to obtain housing, I will very soon open, as a separate category, the ability to apply for a plot even if one's wife or husband has housing. And it has also been decided to open a separate category so that, among those who received plots jointly under the Binveriyaa Scheme opened in 2022, if all those who received the plot agree to give up the plot entirely, every person who received it jointly will get a separate plot. Of the fifteen thousand plots, one thousand plots have been allocated to each of these two categories. The reclamation of Rasmale', where the fifteen thousand plots will be issued, is progressing at a very fast pace. The government's aim, God willing, is to complete the reclamation of Rasmale' by April this year. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; the "Hiyaavehi Financing Scheme", begun to provide financial assistance in the housing sector, is a major advance achieved in the housing sector. Under this scheme, while a total of 2256 forms have been submitted requesting Rashuvehi, Saharu and Fahimale' loans, so far the forms of 821 parties have been approved by the ministry and sent to the bank. The total of these approved loans is more than nine million eighty-nine thousand rufiyaa. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; work is under way to complete and hand over three housing projects [unclear: "last year" as printed]. While the physical work of thirteen housing projects is currently under way, an additional 25 projects have been signed. Among the newly signed projects, eight hundred housing units on thirteen islands under the contractor finance principle, in partnership with Bank of Maldives and contractors,

will begin construction in April this year. Thus, work is under way to build 9175 housing units through housing projects running at various stages at present. God willing, the work on these 9175 housing units will proceed, be completed within the next 26 months, and those projects will be handed over to the people of the islands. At the same time, in August this year, work will begin on building an additional thirteen hundred housing units on various islands. When applications are opened for the housing units being established on the islands, it has also been decided to arrange a set number of housing units so that, among the island's people, those working in the fisheries industry and those working in the tourism industry who need a housing unit can apply. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; among the plots arranged to be issued from Gulhifalhu to those who received plots under the "Binveriyaa" scheme, plot registries have so far been handed over to 2781 parties. In addition, the plots of those who received plots in the Hulhumale' Phase 3 lagoon have been made dry land, a draw was held among them, and plots have been allocated to 689 parties. And the plot draw for all parties who received letters that they would get plots from Giraavarufalhu was held on 31 January 2026. And, God willing, I will complete the reclamation of Giraavarufalhu within the next three months and carry forward handing over plot registries to those who received plots there. In addition, under the "Gedhoruveriyaa" scheme, agreements have been signed with 3850 parties, and flat keys have so far been handed over to 3647 parties. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; under the Inclusive National Affordable Housing principle formulated by the MMA to increase the participation of the Maldives' banking sector in providing housing, it has been made a condition that an amount between 10% and 15% of the loans issued by banks be given for housing at a good price. With this change, the construction work on the affordable housing units newly being built in Hulhumale' by Bank of Maldives has been handed over to two international companies and three Maldivian companies. Under this project, God willing, work will begin on constructing 3260 housing units in Hulhumale' and Vilimale'. God willing, all these units will be completed within the next thirty months and those flats will be

handed over to those who will receive them. The buildings constructed under this social housing scheme, built with land given free by the government, will go to those selected under the social housing scheme. At the same time, among the work done to increase the participation of the Maldives' banking sector in providing housing, the equity on loans taken from Bank of Maldives to buy a house or flat has been reduced to 5% [unclear: "a year" as printed], in line with the government's policy of bringing housing within reach. And the amount that can be borrowed to build a house in Male' has been increased from fifteen million rufiyaa to forty-five million rufiyaa, and the loan repayment period extended from 15 years to 20 years. At the same time, lending of up to three million rufiyaa without additional collateral has begun for building or repairing houses on every island of the Maldives, and the earlier requirement to submit additional collateral to build one's own house has been ended. It has been ended, bringing great relief to the people. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; among the further work the government is doing to resolve the housing difficulties faced by the people, to find easier ways for those who wish to buy houses and those who wish to build or repair houses, the government has now submitted amendments to the Maldives Pension Act to arrange for pension fund money to be collateralised in certain circumstances. As the law currently stands, pension fund money can be used only to pay the down payment for buying a completed house. However, once the amendment now submitted is passed into law, there will be the opportunity to arrange down payment money to buy, build or repair a house through a loan issued by a financial institution. In addition, to establish a housing system through which all citizens living in the Maldives can easily use the opportunities available to attain safe, adequate housing that meets the needs of living, and, under that system, to pave the way for providing places to live to those who most need housing, to set out the principles for registering housing providers and the principles for running such projects, to set the standards and facilities that must exist in places developed under housing projects, and to establish a "Housing Fund" to assist those who need housing, the government has sent a bill named the "Housing Bill" to this Honourable

Majlis. I note with pleasure that the debate on this bill is proceeding at the committee stage. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; the nation's economic and social development and security will be ensured only by establishing peace and stability in the nation and ensuring the safety and security of the people. And providing this assurance is one of the foremost obligations upon me. Accordingly, this government began a major project to expand the services of the Maldives Police, who are entrusted with the greatest responsibility of maintaining public order in society and enforcing the law. And police services have been newly established on 39 islands where the service had not been established at the start of last year. As a result, police are now stationed and providing police services on every inhabited island of the Maldives. In addition, changing the situation in which police had their own stations on only seventeen islands when this government began, 147 projects to build police stations of their own have been contracted and work has begun. This is the time with the most projects running at once to develop the police sector in the history of the Maldives Police Service. God willing, all these projects will be completed within the next fifteen months and police services will begin at those stations. At the same time, work has also begun to review the structure of the police institution. As a result of this work, the extent to which police are active in serving the people will be increased and the quality of investigations raised this year. In addition, the accountability system will be improved more than now, and, God willing, the people's trust and confidence in the police institution will increase. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members; to establish peace and stability in the nation and ensure the safety and security of the people, work is being done on two fronts at once to resolve the drug problem. That is, reducing the supply of drugs, or the availability of drugs in society, and working to save people from the drug epidemic, or to rehabilitate them. To reduce the supply of drugs, 212 operations were carried out in 2025. Among these, as a special operation against those involved in the drug trade, an operation named "Operation Alimagu" has been started throughout the Maldives and is being carried forward. This operation began as a special effort to search a hundred places throughout the Maldives at once using five hundred police officers.

This work is still under way. So far 204 places have been searched, 271 persons arrested, 120 cases investigated, and 37 persons sent for prosecution. As a result of all these operations, a total of 712 kilograms of various kinds of drugs were brought under police custody last year. In addition, 7245 cannabis plants or cannabis stalks were seized. By street value, these items are more than one billion rufiyaa worth of drugs. And since 17 November 2023, 1366 kilograms of drugs and 14825 cannabis plants have been seized so far. The total street value of these items is 2.3 billion Maldivian rufiyaa. I note that, of the past three terms, these are the two years in which the most drugs were seized in the first two years. Likewise, to identify the drug-trafficking networks active in various parts of the Maldives and stop the networks that bring drugs into the Maldives and launder the money earned from trading them, special operations directly targeting such networks have begun. Accordingly, operations targeting drug-trafficking networks in various cities have begun. Those leading these networks and those working prominently under them have been arrested, and their cases are now being investigated. God willing, this operation will be expanded to every atoll throughout the Maldives this year.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

The challenges to the work the government has been doing to save the Maldivian nation from the drug epidemic are many. Therefore, to eliminate those obstacles, important major amendments have been made to the Drug Act. Among these amendments, severe penalties have now been set, including the death penalty, for drug traffickers in cases where the drugs reach a certain weight, where the bench of the Supreme Court rules unanimously.

In addition, with these amendments, the system of treatment provided to persons addicted to drugs has been further strengthened. And the principles for running the Drug Court and the principles related to the Drug Court's treatment programme have been reviewed under this amendment.
