Likewise, additional powers have been given to law enforcement agencies to stop drug-related crimes. The principles for freezing property obtained through crime and for confiscating such property to the state

have also been reviewed through this amendment. Because of these important changes made to the law that I mentioned, remedies have now been found for the obstacles or loopholes previously faced, legally and in matters of drug treatment, in investigating drug cases.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

I give very high priority to establishing a robust system for treating persons addicted to drugs so they can return to society in a good way. Accordingly, since there has until now been inadequate provision of religious lessons within drug rehabilitation treatment, arrangements have now been made, in order to make lessons of complete Islamic upbringing a formal part of the drug rehabilitation programme, for the Risaalath programme run by the Ministry of Islamic Affairs to be conducted by that ministry for young people receiving drug treatment. God willing, this will begin in May this year. And the work of building rehabilitation centres in K. Kaashidhoo, N. Velidhoo and L. Gan has been contracted and the physical work is under way. God willing, the physical work on these three centres will be fully completed and they will be put into treatment service very soon.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

I regard bringing a permanent solution to the problem of crime committed by forming gangs, believed to be directly and indirectly connected to drugs, as something that must be done to establish stability, peace and safety in this nation. Accordingly, I note that since the law that began to be enforced last year came into being, gang activity has decreased and many young people who were involved in it are working to distance themselves from it. And the government will welcome such young people and provide every opportunity that must be provided for them to live as responsible citizens. However, if anyone, even after the law came in, operates as a gang in the criminal environment, I will take action in accordance with the provisions of the law. Accordingly, for the first time in the history of the Maldives, an identified group has been sent to the Prosecutor General's Office to be designated a gang under the new law on preventing gang crimes. And that office has also submitted the case to the High Court. In addition, a request has also been sent for the Commissioner of Sports to be ordered to dissolve a club believed to belong to such a group.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

Another area in which real, sustainable positive change must be brought in establishing peace and safety in society is the area of providing the rehabilitative treatment and assistance needed by children at risk of falling into crime and children who come to fall into crime for various reasons. Looking at this, under the Juvenile Justice Act brought into being in 2019, the Juvenile Residential Treatment Centre and the Juvenile Halfway House, two important centres required to be established within eighteen months, had still not been established by the government of the time even four years after that law. However, this government has established these two centres and they have now begun providing service. The treatment programmes needed for children rescued from the criminal environment to return to society are now being run from the centres I mentioned. The start of these centres' services is a very great advance in providing the treatment and assistance needed for children rescued from the criminal environment to return to society.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

Saving young people and children from drugs, violence, gang crimes and other bad acts, and making those young people and children a beneficial, useful people, is the responsibility of a state. I regard it as specifically the responsibility of the government. Accordingly, the area that must be given the highest priority is the upbringing of young people. Tomorrow this beloved homeland will travel in the direction set by today's young people, by the energy of those young people. Therefore, ending the neglect of the young generation for ages, in the first batch of the Dhivehi National Movement training programme, a special work this government began to build a robust young generation, 344 young people were trained and graduated on 28 December 2025. Of these, 65 selected young people began the technical training of the Dhivehi National Service on 15 January this year at the Technical and Vocational Education Centre in B. Atoll Kihaadhoo. For the graduates not selected for these trainings, the government has arranged jobs at the places where they expressed interest in working. Accordingly, jobs have been arranged for 171 young people in the MNDF, 7 as MNDF auxiliary firemen, 32 in the Aviation and Port Security Command, 23 in the Maldives Police Service, 5 in Maldives Immigration, and 3 in MACL.

As 38 young people wished to work in the private sector, they have been given that opportunity and released.

For the second batch of Dhivehi National Service training, 350 young people have now departed to Maafilaafushi on 24 January. The government's aim is to give an additional one thousand young people the opportunity to complete the Dhivehi National Movement training this year. God willing, that will be achieved.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

To entertain young people, give them artistic skills in the arts, empower civil society organisations and instil a spirit of reading and learning among young people, the Youth Hub was opened, and so far 680 young people have obtained services in the various programmes provided by the facilities prepared there.

The work of establishing such youth hubs in all cities, to run various skills programmes connected to young people and to plan and organise various activities specifically for young people, has now been handed over. In addition, land needed to establish such youth hubs in GA. Vilingili, HA. Dhidhdhoo, ADh. Mahibadhoo, B. Eydhafushi, Dh. Kudahuvadhoo, F. Nilandhoo, L. Fonadhoo, Lh. Naifaru and R. Ungoofaaru has been arranged, and, God willing, the physical work will begin this year.

And, to empower young people, it has also been arranged to train young people in the field of the arts, to hold a National Youth Conference, and to create a Youth Parliament including young people from various constituencies of various islands. In addition, to increase youth participation and inclusion, with the start of work to seek young people's views on various matters run by government ministries, reintegration activities targeting young people have begun. And it has also been decided to start a special programme to increase religious awareness among young people in order to save them from the criminal environment and eliminate extremist thought.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

Bringing a comprehensive solution in establishing stability in the nation is an extreme necessity. Accordingly, when those sentenced to prison for committing crimes are held in prison, it is very important to ensure that arrangements are in place consistent with human dignity and international standards. Looking at it this way, on 17 November 2023

offenders in many cells of the Maldives' prisons were living without electricity. Among the work done to improve the conditions of prisoners, electricity has now been supplied to the cells of all prisons. To stop the practice of committing crimes by bringing prohibited items into prisons, a state-of-the-art body scanner has now been taken to Maafushi Prison. This scanner will be installed, training given, and it will begin to be used in April this year. As a result, God willing, scam calls from prison and other such matters can be brought to a halt.

It is my policy to change prison, instead of a place one is taken only for punishment, into a place where prisoners serving sentences are given the opportunity of reformative rehabilitation to make them successful people in life. Accordingly, the policy has now been changed so that, by regularly participating in rehabilitation programmes and maintaining conduct at a certain standard, an additional day is deducted from the prison sentence for every day spent in the programme. And for the first time in the history of the Maldives, it has been decided to develop an island focused on rehabilitation on the open prison island concept, designating a whole island as a prison where prisoners can live and work, and it has been handed over to the Maldives Correctional Service. And it is planned to begin the infrastructure work needed to establish this prison in the middle of this year and to place prisoners there by the end of this year. Those taken to this island will be persons imprisoned in minor cases requiring minimum security. These persons can be taught agriculture and other such work on this island.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

There is one policy included in carrying forward all the matters connected to the people that I have described. That is the policy of working on decentralised principles, close to the people, listening to the people, to reach the goals the people desire. At the same time, empowering councils financially through the decentralised system is also a policy of this government. Uninhabited islands have been opened for councils to obtain as a means of gaining financial well-being. While 27 uninhabited islands have been allocated for this, twelve councils submitted fifteen proposals to obtain some of those islands. I note that seven islands have so far been issued to 6 councils. With the important purpose of providing the services the general public needs as close to the people as possible, in a decentralised manner, in an easy and convenient way, the service of making the card that identifies a Maldivian citizen, and the Maldivian

passport service, available from all inhabited atolls of the Maldives, this service was begun in 2025 in every inhabited atoll of the Maldives, as part of the work started to arrange that. In addition, in populous atolls, the national identity card and passport service has begun on more than one island. I note with pleasure that, because these services have been decentralised and expanded in this way, the hardship citizens previously bore to obtain the service has been reduced many times over, the costs citizens incurred for it have been reduced many-fold, and citizens are receiving the service with ease and speed.

At the same time, because self-service banking ATMs have been established on every inhabited island of the Maldives and that service decentralised, arrangements are now in place for various services such as depositing money, withdrawing money, transferring money and paying credit cards and loans to be easily available while staying on the island. At the same time, dollar ATMs have been opened on seven islands for the first time, and the work needed to place dollar ATMs on an additional 70 islands has begun. God willing, I will place these 70 ATMs and begin providing service by the end of March this year.

In addition, the work the government is doing to improve the physical condition of council offices, the buildings used on the islands to provide decentralised services to the people, and to resolve the shortage of space, are also projects carried forward to strengthen the decentralised system. Accordingly, in 2025 the physical work of building 55 council offices began. When the project is completed, everything needed to provide services will be complete in the offices. God willing, the work on those 55 council offices will be completed this year and they will begin serving the people. At the same time, the work on 6 council offices under the PSIP run by the government has been completed. And the physical work of building 19 council offices is still under way. In addition, the feasibility study of the project of 50 council offices to be built with grant aid from the Government of China has been completed. Finding land on which to build the council offices and other administrative work is now under way.

And the work needed to increase the space required to run the councils in Addu Hulhudhoo and Addu Meedhoo, the two councils newly being formed by the people's vote, will begin this month. And, God willing, I will carry forward as soon as possible the recruitment of the administrative staff needed for the two councils and the staff needed to strengthen municipal services.

In addition, to further develop the atoll shops in Male' and make them a place from which many benefits can be given to the people of the atolls, God willing, I will open in the middle of this year, to parties wishing to invest in partnership with the government, the redevelopment of the area where the atoll shop row stands into a modern commercial front. Since the atoll shop row is a heritage of many ages as a symbol of Male's waterfront, I intend to carry forward this redevelopment project in a way that keeps the outer wall of the atoll shop building protected for the long term.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

Raising the government's efficiency in serving the people and establishing a modern digitalisation system built on the principles of good governance is something it has been decided to give very high priority this year. When this is achieved, the result will be a change to a trusted system of service that is easy for the citizens receiving the service, light for the state employees providing the service, fast, transparent and leaving no room for corruption. This is a revolutionary positive change to the administrative system by which the Maldivian state has been run since ancient times. Under Maldives 2.0, inaugurated on 21 May 2025, within the next three years, God willing, I will complete: strengthening cyber security together with all institutions of the Maldivian state; paving the way for trustworthy, reliable digital transactions through a digital ID meeting international standards; arranging for data to be sent securely in real time between state institutions; establishing the Maldives Data Exchange; establishing a sovereign cloud to manage and archive the sensitive information of state institutions securely; making the services provided by the state citizen-centric and paving the way to provide those services digitally under one roof; and building a generation ready for the future in the digital field. To run this project, a roadmap for the digital transformation project has been drafted and passed by the Cabinet. Special priority has been given in this year's budget to implementing this roadmap. To establish the legal framework needed to carry forward this nationally run project quickly, God willing, I will submit a bill on digital transformation, a bill on digital identity and a bill on cyber security to this Honourable Majlis in the first session this year.

Under Maldives 2.0, the government's aim is, by the end of this year, to establish a single network for providing civil registration services in the Maldives and to make the Maldives the country providing civil registration services most completely at the regional level. With this, the standard of the national identity card will be improved and, with major changes, God willing, the national identity card will change to a smart card.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

I believe that once the system of running the state is digitalised, the epidemic of corruption will very largely disappear from the system of running the state. This government is doing a great deal of work to eliminate corruption. Accordingly, preparations are under way to submit the relevant bills to this Honourable Majlis in the first session of this year. Accordingly, it has been decided to submit a bill to amend the Anti-Corruption Act, a bill on asset recovery, and a bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act.

In addition to these bills, it is certain that once the bill to amend the Penal Code of the Maldives regarding the offence of illicit enrichment and the bill to amend the Evidence Act, which are at the committee stage of this Honourable Majlis, are passed, much progress will be made towards resolving this major problem. And the assurance I give to you, Honourable Members of the Majlis, is that if the case of any party committing corruption, theft and wrongdoing is brought to me with the evidence of that case, I will not hesitate in the slightest in taking the action that must be taken against that party.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

I regard the existence of an independent judiciary as an essential, fundamental requirement in ensuring stability and safety in the nation. Accordingly, in addition to beginning last year to run the Criminal Court and the Drug Court, which had become dilapidated and unusable, in a spacious, quality building in Hulhumale', full independence has been given to the judicial sector in implementing that sector's budget. In this year's budget, 808 million rufiyaa, 2% of the revenue projected for this year, has been included as the judiciary sectoral grant. This is a budget two hundred million rufiyaa larger than the six hundred million rufiyaa budget spent on the judicial sector by the end of 2025. Full independence in implementing this budget has been guaranteed in line with the provisions of public finance management.

And the principles drafted in this regard were gazetted on 19 January this year. And, God willing, this year I will also begin the work of constructing a superior court complex in Hulhumale'.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

As a further very important step taken in proceeding as a government run as close as possible to the people, listening to the people, I announce that it has been decided to establish at the President's Office a 24-hour office named the Citizens' Complaints Bureau, an office for submitting the people's concerns and complaints.

The main responsibility of this bureau is to arrange for complaints submitted by citizens through various platforms such as letters, email, Raiyithunge Adu, the GEMS messaging platform, phone and social media to be managed through a digital system, to obtain the information that must be obtained from the relevant government offices regarding those complaints, and to respond to those complaints. A state-of-the-art automated digital system designed to include artificial intelligence, which will manage complaints, will be established at this centre. Arrangements will be in place for all complaints submitted to the government through various platforms to be recorded in this system, a ticket raised for every complaint, and the progress of every complaint tracked through the system until it is answered. As part of this bureau I will establish a "call centre" providing 24-hour service. At the same time, arrangements will be in place for the separate government offices to use the "Citizens' Complaints Bureau" digital system to manage complaints submitted to them and respond to those complaints, and for complaints submitted to all government offices to be managed through "one single complaints management mechanism". And the "Citizens' Complaints Bureau" will act as an overarching office that monitors how the separate government offices act on and respond to complaints submitted to them, and holds those offices responsible and accountable. In recruiting the staff who will work in this bureau, instead of hiring many additional staff, it has been decided to transfer suitable staff from among those already working at the President's Office and various government offices, give them relevant training

and fully prepare them for the work. God willing, I will establish this office within the next five months and begin serving the people.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

Having a robust media established in the nation is extremely important in establishing stability in the nation, in disclosing the pace of development to the people, and in ensuring safety for the people. Having a responsible media that provides the people with completely truthful news and information while always upholding the standards that must be upheld in a one-hundred-percent Islamic society is a right of the people. Therefore, this government will remain steadfast in ensuring this important right of the people. Accordingly, for the first time in the history of the Maldives, we have released money from the state budget to the media. More than twenty-seven million rufiyaa has now been deposited to forty media outlets. Since media outlets are compelled to rent office and studio space from private buildings at high rents, to pave the way for them to overcome this difficult financial situation and further develop and advance the media with the income they receive, work on the Media Village, which includes office and studio space that can be rented at a very low price, is progressing at a very fast pace. The Media Village being built in Hulhumale' Phase 1 includes 34 spaces. God willing, I will complete this place and open the opportunity for media outlets to use it in the middle of this year.

And likewise, this government will continue to work closely with the media in sharing information with the media. Last year, in sharing the government's activities and answering questions, ministers directly went 424 times to various media, including local and foreign media, to give information and interviews. In addition, on 493 occasions various senior officials of ministries shared various important information the people need through the media.

In addition, if members of the public have information they wish to clarify, on submitting a form requesting it, all government offices are disclosing the requested information to the widest extent that can be disclosed within legal limits. Accordingly, during last year, 1341 RTI requests were sent to the President's Office and ministries, of which 1251 RTIs have been answered and closed. This means 93% of the RTIs sent to the President's Office and ministries have been answered. Because of information that must be gathered at various stages of

preparing answers and the need to extend time for various reasons, answers are still being prepared for the RTI forms not yet answered. This work continues every single day without stopping. So there is not the slightest obstacle to obtaining information for the mass media, print media and individuals.

In addition, to deliver information on various matters to the people through various social media platforms as well, the government published information through 40875 social media posts in 2025.

To further strengthen the close, friendly relationship I have been maintaining with the media, as a way of giving information directly to the media myself, from March this year, as a general practice, God willing, I will meet journalists every week on Monday from 10:00 to 11:00 in the morning. I state that, God willing, I will continue to do this as long as no travel, holiday or other matter arises that changes this schedule.

Likewise, from March this year, every Cabinet minister will meet journalists once a week for one hour. The schedule of these meetings will be published by the President's Office. Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

I regard one of the things causing the greatest hardship to the beloved Maldivian people as the direction in which the nation is travelling changing every five years. Therefore, regarding setting and passing the nation's direction for twenty years, towards the goal the people desire after listening to the people, and giving that direction legal force, as one of the most constructive and most meaningful things that can be done for the development, stability and safety of this nation, I made that pledge in the presidential election. And work to fulfil that pledge has begun, and by the will of God very great progress has been achieved up to today. Accordingly, views have been obtained from a total of ten thousand and eighty [unclear: number garbled in the minutes] parties. Among these, a total of 192 public meetings were held on every inhabited island, 96 focus group meetings were held on the inhabited islands of the Maldives including young people, women, business people, fishermen and farmers, and with state-owned companies, private companies and NGOs

67 meetings were held, meetings were also held with Honourable Members of the People's Majlis and with cooperating political parties, and consultations were held on 62 topics. 20 sector roundtable consultations and meetings with 40 government and state institutions were held. With the views received in all these meetings, the outline of the twenty-year national development plan has now been completed. Next in this important work is holding regional-level validation meetings. It has been decided to hold these meetings by the end of May this year. The purpose of these meetings is to ensure that this plan was prepared with everyone's participation and to secure the cooperation of the people and all parties in implementing it.

After this work, God willing, a national conference will be held before the end of June this year. The main purpose of this conference is to formally establish that this is the development "roadmap" for the coming years, prepared with the participation of the whole of the Maldives. To achieve this, the views coming from the regional validation workshops will be checked for whether they fit the state's financial capacity and the government's main policies, and, with the final decisions taken, work will be done to link the development plans of various sectors towards one goal and to ensure that what is done in one sector does not burden another sector. After this stage, the final plan, drafted together with the implementation and monitoring framework of the twenty-year national development plan, will be completed before the end of July this year.

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, Honourable Members;

This government will proceed on the pledges made to the people for this government to come to power. On the trust the people placed in this government. That is built upon the Islamic framework. Upon the foundation of Maldivian nationhood. Upon the safety and security of Maldivians. Upon modern scientific awareness and productivity. Upon the self-sufficiency, ease of living, peace, equality, trust and peace of mind the people receive.

We have established political stability in this nation in the true sense. And in the days ahead too, what will be seen from this government is the implementation of this policy. God willing, what you will see from now on too is,

justice being established without discriminating against any Maldivian citizen. The Maldivian nation and the Maldives being brought to new heights in thought and knowledge, and in construction and infrastructure.

This is the Maldives of Maldivians! This is the government of Maldivians! The government of the Maldivian people! This government will always be on the side of the people. Together with the people.

God willing, I and the whole of today's government will sacrifice our energy and courage night and day in ensuring development, stability and safety for the beloved Maldivian people.

In this way, may Almighty Allah bless this sincere, boundless work being done seeking benefit and gain for the Maldivian nation in every sense! May He always grant success to the beloved Maldivian people and the Maldivian state! May He make development, stability and safety the everlasting joy of Maldivians! Amen! [Arabic, garbled in the minutes: "My success is only through Allah; in Him I trust and to Him I turn."]

[Arabic, garbled in the minutes: "Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings."]

speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒަށް ވަރަށް އިޚުލާޞްތެރިކަމާ އެކު ޝުކުރު ދަންނަވަން. މަނިކުފާނު މި އިއްޒަތްތެރި މަޖިލީހަށް ތިޔަ ހުށަހަޅުއްވައިދެއްވި ރިޔާސީ ބަޔާނުގައި ފާހަގަކުރެއްވި ކަންތައްތަކުގެ ތެރެއިން ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުން ކުރަންޖެހޭ ކަންކަން ކުރުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީން ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހާ މަތިކޮށްފައިވާ މަސްއޫލިއްޔަތާއި ޒިންމާ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުން ފުރިހަމައަށް އަދާކުރާނެކަމުގެ ޔަގީންކަން އަރުވަން. ވިހިވަނަ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ އަމާޒަކީ ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީން މި މަޖިލީހާ މަތިކޮށްފައިވާ މަސްއޫލިއްޔަތު ފުރިހަމައަށް އަދާކުރަމުން ގެންދިއުން. ވިހިވަނަ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ ވިސްނުމަކީ، ދައުލަތުން ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ފޯރުކޮށްދޭ ޚިދުމަތްތައް ފޯރުކޮށްދެއްވުމުގައި ގާނޫނީ އެއްވެސް ހުރަހެއް އޮތް ކަމަށް ވަންޏާ، ގާނޫނީ އިމުގެ ތެރެއިން އެ ހުރަހަކަށް ޙައްލު ގެނެސްދިނުން. ވިހިވަނަ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ ބޭނުމަކީ، ދިވެހީންގެ ކުރިއެރުމާއި، ދިވެހީންގެ ތަރައްޤީއާއި، ދިވެހީންގެ ޖަމަޖެހުމަށް ޓަކައި ކުރަންޖެހޭ މަސައްކަތް ވަރުބަލިކަމެއް ނެތި ކުރަމުންގެންދިއުން. ވިހިވަނަ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުން އަބަދުވެސް އިސްކުރާނީ ދިވެހީންގެ ޤައުމާއި ދިވެހީން، ދިވެހީންގެ ކުރިއެރުން، ދިވެހީންގެ ތަރައްޤީ، ދިވެހީންގެ ހަމަޖެހުން،
ދިވެހީންގެ ރައްކާތެރިކަން. އަޅުގަނޑު، ރައީސް ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒަށް ޔަގީންކަން އަރުވަން ބޭނުންވަނީ، މި ވިހިވަނަ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލިސް ދެމިއޮންނާނީ ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި، ދިވެހި ދައުލަތާއި، ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނާއި، ދިވެހީންނާ އެކީގައި. އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރުން ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ މަސައްކަތުގައި ކޮށްދެއްވާ ތިޔަ ބުރަ މަސައްކަތަށް ވަރަށް އިޚްލާޞްތެރިކަމާ އެކީގައި ތިޔަ ހުރިހާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރުންނަށް ޝުކުރު ދަންނަވަން. ކުރިއަށް މި އޮތް އަހަރަކީ ވެސް ޥޭތުވެގެންދިޔަ އަހަރެކޭ އެއްފަދައިން މި މަޖިލީހުން އުފެއްދުންތެރި، ބިނާކުރަނިވި، ހަރުދަނާ މަސައްކަތްތަކެއް ކުރަން ހުރި، އަދި ކުރެވިގެންދާނެ އަހަރެއް ކަމަށް ވެގެންދާނެކަމާ މެދަކު އަޅުގަނޑު ޝައްކެއްނުކުރަން. އަދި މި މަސައްކަތުގައި ތިޔަ ހުރިހާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރުންގެ ފުރިހަމަ އެހީތެރިކަމާއި އެއްބާރުލުން ލިބޭނެކަމާ މެދު ޔަގީންކުރަން. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ މި މަސައްކަތުގައި މާތްﷲ ސުބުޙާނަހޫ ވަތަޢާލާގެ ހެޔޮ ރަޙުމަތް މިންވަރުކުރައްވައި، އަޅުގަނޑުމެން އެންމެން ގުޅިގެން މިކުރާ މަސައްކަތުގައި ކާމިޔާބީ މިންވަރުކުރައްވާށި! އަދި މި ލޮބުވެތި ދިވެހި ޤައުމުގެ ހެވާއި ލާބަޔަށް ޓަކައި ވަރުގަދަ ޢަޒުމަކާ އެކު މަސައްކަތްކުރުމުގެ ހެޔޮ ތައުފީޤު ދެއްވާށި! އާމީން! ދެން މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖަލްސާއެއް އޮންނާނީ 9 ފެބުރުވަރީ 2026 ވާ ހޯމަ ދުވަހުގެ ހެނދުނު 9:00ގައި.
والحمد للهّ رب العالمين . މަޖިލިސް ނިމުނީ.
____________
speeches.en:
I thank the Honourable President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu with great sincerity. I assure you that, in doing what the People's Majlis must do among the matters highlighted in the presidential address you have presented to this Honourable Majlis, the People's Majlis will fully discharge the responsibility and duty that the Constitution of the Maldives has placed on the People's Majlis. The aim of the 20th People's Majlis is to keep fully discharging the responsibility the Constitution has placed on this Majlis. The thinking of the 20th People's Majlis is that, if there is any legal obstacle to the State delivering services to the people, it should resolve that obstacle within the legal framework. The purpose of the 20th People's Majlis is to keep doing, tirelessly, the work that must be done for the advancement of Maldivians, the development of Maldivians and the stability of Maldivians. The 20th People's Majlis will always put first the nation of Maldivians and Maldivians, the advancement of Maldivians, the development of Maldivians, the stability of Maldivians,

the security of Maldivians. What I want to assure President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu is that this 20th People's Majlis will stand together with the Maldivian government, the Maldivian state, the Maldivian people and Maldivians. I thank all you Honourable Members with great sincerity for the hard work you do in the work of the People's Majlis. I have no doubt that the coming year too, like the year that has passed, will be a year in which this Majlis has productive, constructive and robust work to do, and will get it done. I am also certain that all you Honourable Members will give your full help and cooperation in this work. May Almighty Allah, Glorified and Exalted, decree His good mercy upon this work of ours and grant success to the work we are all doing together! And may He grant us the good fortune to work with strong resolve for the good and benefit of this beloved Maldivian nation! Amen! The next sitting of the Majlis will be held at 9:00 in the morning on Monday, 9 February 2026.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Majlis is adjourned.
